arguments.content:
# Research: Training a <100M LLM That Punches Toward Gemma-class Quality

Two sections: **Papers** (real, with links) and **Ideas** (things that could work for us).
Theme: cram maximum capability and knowledge into a tiny model.

---

## Section 1: Papers (35)

# TinyStories: How Small Can Language Models Be and Still Speak Coherent English?
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759
- Shows models under 10M params produce coherent, grammatical English when trained on a curated synthetic dataset matched to a constrained vocabulary. The founding result that data design — not parameter count — sets the floor for fluency. Core evidence for our whole project.

# Textbooks Are All You Need (phi-1)
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11644
- 1.3B model trained on "textbook-quality" filtered + synthetic data hits 50.6% HumanEval, beating far larger models. Proof that data quality bends scaling laws hard enough that a tiny model can compete out of its weight class.

# Textbooks Are All You Need II: phi-1.5 Technical Report
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05463
- phi-1.5 (1.3B) matches models 5x larger on natural-language tasks and beats most non-frontier LLMs on grade-school math and coding. Extends the textbook-data recipe from code to general reasoning.

# MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14905
- The architecture bible for our scale: deep-and-thin beats wide-and-shallow at 125M/350M; embedding sharing, grouped-query attention, and block-wise weight sharing give +2.7%/4.3% accuracy over prior SOTA. Shows architecture matters most at sub-billion scale.

# MobileLLM-R1: Exploring the Limits of Sub-Billion Language Model Reasoners with Open Training Recipes
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24945
- 360M model beats SmolLM2-1.7B on reasoning using fully open training recipes. Direct evidence that a sub-500M model can outperform a 1.7B with the right data and post-training.

# Small Language Models: Survey, Measurements, and Insights
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15790
- Surveys 70 open SLMs (100M–5B): architectures, data, training algorithms, on-device cost measurements. The map of the design space we're operating in.

# A Survey of Small Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.20011
- Complementary survey covering compression, distillation, quantization, and training strategies specifically for small models. Good source of cross-cutting technique comparisons.

# What is the Role of Small Models in the LLM Era: A Survey
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06857
- Frames where small models genuinely win (latency, specialization, privacy) vs. where they need help from larger models. Useful for scoping which capabilities to even target.

# Super Tiny Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14159
- Research program targeting 10M/50M/100M models: tokenizer-free approaches, self-play training, alternative objectives, weight tying. Directly aimed at our exact parameter budget.

# Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network (Hinton et al.)
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531
- The original distillation paper: soft teacher targets carry "dark knowledge" (relative probabilities of wrong answers) that hard labels don't. Foundation of every teacher→student plan we have.

# DistilBERT: a distilled version of BERT
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.01108
- 40% smaller, keeps 97% of BERT's capability via logit distillation + cosine embedding loss during pretraining. The classic existence proof that most of a model's quality survives heavy compression.

# MiniLM: Deep Self-Attention Distillation
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10957
- Distills only the last layer's self-attention relations (Q-K and V-V) instead of matching all hidden states — student architecture becomes free to differ from teacher. Highly relevant since our student is much smaller than any teacher.

# MiniLLM: Knowledge Distillation of Large Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543
- Replaces forward KL with reverse KL for generative distillation, so the student doesn't waste capacity on the teacher's low-probability tail. Exactly the fix needed when student capacity is tiny.

# Baby Llama: knowledge distillation from an ensemble of teachers trained on a small dataset
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.02019
- 58M-param student distilled from an ensemble of teachers beats both teachers trained on the same 10M-word corpus. Distillation outperforms direct pretraining at exactly our scale.

# Revealing the Power of Post-Training for Small Language Models via Knowledge Distillation
- https://arxiv.org/html/2509.26497
- Systematic study of distillation-based post-training pipelines for SLMs — what to distill (logits, data, reasoning traces) at which stage. A recipe paper for our post-training phase.

# Orca 2: Teaching Small Language Models How to Reason
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.11045
- Trains small models on varied reasoning strategies and teaches them to pick a strategy per task, instead of imitating teacher answers verbatim. "Cautious reasoning" beats naive imitation for small students.

# Rephrasing the Web (WRAP): A Recipe for Compute & Data-Efficient Language Modeling
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16380
- LLM-rephrased web text gives 3x pretraining speedup; a 350M model on 15% of rephrased C4 beats a 1.3B trained on all of raw C4. The single highest-leverage data trick for a small compute budget.

# The FineWeb Datasets: Decanting the Web for the Finest Text Data at Scale
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17557
- 15T tokens of carefully filtered/deduped Common Crawl; FineWeb-Edu subset (1.3T tokens of educational text) dramatically improves MMLU/ARC. Our default high-quality base corpus.

# DataComp-LM: In search of the next generation of training sets for language models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.11794
- 240T-token benchmark for data curation; model-based filtering (DCLM-Baseline) gets +6.6 MMLU points with 40% less compute. Tells us which filtering strategies actually pay off.

# Ultra-FineWeb: Efficient Data Filtering and Verification for High-Quality LLM Training Data
- https://arxiv.org/html/2505.05427v1
- Cheap verification loop for data classifiers — validate filters by actually training small models, then re-filter. A practical pipeline we can run ourselves at small scale.

# Physics of Language Models: Part 3.3, Knowledge Capacity Scaling Laws
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405
- Measures knowledge storage: transformers store ~2 bits per parameter when trained well; quantization, architecture, training duration, and junk-data ratio all shift capacity. Gives us a hard budget: ~100M params ≈ ~25MB of facts — so spend them wisely.

# Language models scale reliably with over-training and on downstream tasks
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08540
- Scaling laws hold far past Chinchilla-optimal token counts; overtraining small models is predictable and worthwhile when inference cost matters. License to train our 100M model on 100x "too many" tokens.

# Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556
- The canonical compute-optimal scaling law (≈20 tokens/param). We deliberately violate it by overtraining — but it's the baseline every data-budget decision is measured against.

# ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11942
- Cross-layer parameter sharing + factorized embeddings: SOTA results with 70% fewer parameters than BERT. The classic recipe for buying effective depth without parameter cost.

# Universal Transformers
- https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03819
- One shared block applied repeatedly matches deep non-shared stacks, with adaptive computation time per token. The ancestor of looped/recurrent-depth models — depth via iteration, not parameters.

# Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171
- 3.5B model that "thinks" by looping a recurrent block in latent space at inference, scaling to the equivalent of 50B-param compute. Test-time depth-looping is a parameter-free way for a tiny model to think harder.

# BitNet b1.58 Reloaded: State-of-the-art Performance Also on Smaller Networks
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09527
- Shows 1.58-bit (ternary weight) quantization-aware training works at small model scale, not just 3B+. Means our 100M budget could be a ~400M-param ternary model in the same memory footprint.

# Continual Quantization-Aware Pre-Training: When to transition from 16-bit to 1.58-bit
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11895
- 16-bit warm-start then switch to 1.58-bit QAT beats full ternary-from-scratch across 11 tasks. The practical training schedule if we go the BitNet route.

# Sheared LLaMA: Accelerating Language Model Pre-training via Structured Pruning
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06694
- Structured-prune a big pretrained model down, then continue training: beats from-scratch models of equal size at ~3% of the compute. Possibly the cheapest path to a strong 100M model — shear something good instead of starting cold.

# Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens (RETRO)
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.04426
- 7B model + retrieval from a 2T-token database matches GPT-3 175B (25x larger) on the Pile. Retrieval is external knowledge storage — the model only needs to learn reasoning and language, not facts.

# Retro-li: Small-Scale Retrieval Augmented Generation
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00004
- Brings RETRO-style retrieval to small models with small databases (570K–2.89B tokens), plus noise-regularized neighbor embeddings for domain shift. Retrieval validated at exactly our scale.

# Memory³: Language Modeling with Explicit Memory
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.01178
- Adds a third memory tier (explicit, sparse key-value memory) between weights and context; a 2.4B model with explicit memory beats larger conventional models. Blueprint for divorcing knowledge storage from parameter count.

# Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871
- Tokenizer-free byte model with entropy-based dynamic patching matches subword models while cutting inference FLOPs. Eliminates the embedding table — which at 100M scale can eat a third of the parameter budget.

# Over-Tokenized Transformer: Vocabulary is Generally Worth Scaling
- https://arxiv.org/html/2501.16975v1
- Decouples input vs. output vocab; scaling input vocabulary improves performance at near-zero compute cost. Tells us where the embedding budget actually pays — input side, not output side.

# Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09629
- Model learns to generate internal rationales between tokens, improving reasoning without external supervision. A way to convert extra training compute into reasoning ability without adding parameters.

---

## Section 2: Ideas That Could Work (100)

### Data (1–20)

# 1. Full-synthetic "textbook curriculum" corpus
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11644)
- Generate the entire pretraining corpus with a frontier model as a graded K-12-to-undergrad textbook series: definitions, worked examples, exercises, solutions. No raw web at all. Maximizes facts-per-token for a model that can only afford ~2B unique tokens.

# 2. WRAP-style rephrase everything 4 ways
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16380)
- Rephrase each source document into 4 registers (textbook, QA pairs, dialogue, summary). Same facts, multiple surface forms — teaches the knowledge, not the phrasing, and multiplies effective dataset size.

# 3. Fact-density filtering
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405)
- Score every document by named entities + verifiable claims per 100 tokens; train only on the top slice. With ~2 bits/param capacity, every low-density token is wasted budget.

# 4. Train a 10M-param data filter ensemble
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.11794)
- DCLM showed model-based filtering wins. At our scale we can afford to validate filters empirically: train 10M proxy models on candidate data slices, keep filters whose slices yield the best proxies.

# 5. Knowledge-graph-to-text generation
- (idea)
- Walk Wikidata triples, render each entity neighborhood as fluent text in several phrasings. Guarantees uniform coverage of core world facts instead of web data's popularity skew.

# 6. Spaced-repetition data scheduling
- (idea)
- Show each fact-bearing document at increasing intervals during training (epoch 1, 3, 9, 27...) instead of uniform shuffling. Mirrors human memory consolidation; fights the catastrophic forgetting that hits small models hardest.

# 7. Curriculum: TinyStories → FineWeb-Edu → reasoning traces
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17557)
- Three-stage curriculum: simple coherent language first, dense knowledge second, reasoning last. Each stage initializes the next; grammar is cheap to learn early and expensive to learn late.

# 8. Aggressive semantic dedup with one-shot exceptions
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17557)
- SemDeDup-style removal of near-duplicates, but deliberately keep 2–3 paraphrase variants of high-value facts (idea #2). Dedup junk, multiply gold.

# 9. Decay-resistant "core knowledge" replay buffer
- (idea)
- Hold out a 100M-token distilled core (definitions, math facts, common-sense assertions) and mix 5% of it into every training stage including finetuning. Anchor against forgetting.

# 10. Negative-knowledge data
- (idea)
- Include explicit "common misconception → correction" pairs. Small models hallucinate confidently; training directly on error-vs-truth contrasts may buy calibration cheaply.

# 11. Code as reasoning scaffold, even for a non-code model
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11644)
- Include 10–15% simple Python even if code generation isn't a goal — code's explicit state and control flow measurably improves natural-language reasoning in small models.

# 12. Tool-call traces in pretraining
- (idea)
- Pretrain on synthetic traces of calculator/search/lookup tool use. A 100M model shouldn't memorize arithmetic or rare facts — it should learn to delegate. Bakes the interface in early.

# 13. Multi-hop QA chains as a first-class data type
- (idea)
- Synthesize questions whose answers require chaining 2–3 facts that appear in separate documents, with the chain spelled out. Forces knowledge-composition circuits a small model won't form on its own.

# 14. Definition-first vocabulary injection
- (idea)
- For every token in the tokenizer vocab, include dictionary-style definition + example sentences. Guarantees no token is undertrained — a known failure mode in small models with big vocabs.

# 15. Compression-as-filtering
- (idea)
- Use gzip/LLM-perplexity agreement to drop both incompressible noise and trivially compressible boilerplate; keep the mid-band where information lives. Cheap, scalable, model-free first pass.

# 16. Self-correction traces from teacher failures
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14523v1)
- Collect cases where a mid-size model errs and a frontier model corrects it; train on the full error→critique→fix trace. Teaches recovery behavior, which matters more for weak models than strong ones.

# 17. Domain-stratified token budget
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405)
- Allocate the token budget explicitly (e.g., 40% general knowledge, 20% reasoning, 15% code, 15% dialogue, 10% math) and enforce per-domain dedup, rather than letting web priors set the mix. At fixed capacity, the data mix IS the model spec.

# 18. Frontier-model "exam writing" for eval-driven curation
- (idea)
- Have a frontier model write thousands of exam questions per domain; measure checkpoint accuracy per domain; reweight next data mix toward weak areas. Closed-loop data curriculum.

# 19. Train on Gemma's actual outputs across a broad prompt set
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)
- The target is "close to Gemma E4B quality" — so make Gemma the data generator: millions of prompts, sampled Gemma responses as targets. Direct behavioral cloning of the reference model.

# 20. Long-tail amputation
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405)
- Deliberately exclude rare entities (below a Wikipedia pageview threshold) from pretraining and route those to retrieval (idea #41). Don't spend scarce bits on facts almost no user will ask.

### Architecture (21–40)

# 21. Deep-and-thin baseline: ~40 layers, ~512 width
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14905)
- MobileLLM's central finding applied to 100M: maximize depth at fixed budget. Start near 40 layers × 512 dim with GQA and tied embeddings; ablate from there.

# 22. Looped middle block (2–4 iterations)
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03819 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171)
- Keep unique entry/exit layers, loop the middle stack 2–4 times with shared weights. Effective depth 60+ at the parameter cost of ~20 layers.

# 23. Adaptive loop count at inference (latent test-time compute)
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171)
- Train the looped block with stochastic iteration counts so inference can dial 1–8 loops per difficulty. A 100M model that loops 8x on hard questions rents compute instead of owning parameters.

# 24. Factorized embeddings (ALBERT-style)
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11942)
- Project vocab → 128-dim → model-dim. With a 32k vocab and 512 width, tied factorized embeddings free ~10M+ params for transformer layers.

# 25. Over-tokenized input, small output vocab
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2501.16975v1)
- Large n-gram-augmented input embedding (cheap: lookup only) with a small output softmax. Gets the documented input-vocab gains without paying output-projection compute.

# 26. Byte-level fallback hybrid tokenizer
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871 and https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10322v2)
- Small ~16k subword vocab plus byte-level composition for rare words (hierarchical byte→word encoder). Shrinks embedding table while staying robust to typos and rare strings.

# 27. Per-layer LoRA deltas on a shared block
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.12880)
- One shared transformer block + tiny per-iteration LoRA adapters. 95% of weights shared, but each "layer" can still specialize. Best of ALBERT and standard stacks.

# 28. Product-key memory layer for facts
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.01178)
- Replace one mid FFN with a product-key memory (millions of sparse slots, O(√N) lookup). Sparse memory stores facts far more cheaply per-bit than dense FFN weights — the highest-leverage swap for "stuffing info in."

# 29. Tiny MoE: 8 experts of 8M, top-2 routing
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2605.27358v1)
- ~100M total params but only ~40M active per token. More stored knowledge at the same inference cost; the same trick (per-layer expert routing) that makes Gemma E4B punch above its active-parameter count.

# 30. SSM/attention hybrid for long context on the cheap
- (idea)
- Replace 2/3 of attention layers with Mamba-style SSM blocks; keep a few attention layers for retrieval-within-context. Cuts KV-cache memory so the small model can afford long contexts — its substitute for parametric knowledge.

# 31. Multi-token prediction heads
- (idea)
- Auxiliary heads predicting tokens t+2..t+4 during training (dropped at inference). Documented sample-efficiency gains; free quality at zero deployed-parameter cost.

# 32. Ternary (1.58-bit) 400M ≡ fp16 100M
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09527 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11895)
- If the constraint is really memory/deployment size, train a ~400M-param BitNet ternary model occupying the bytes of a 100M fp16 model. 4x the knowledge slots in the same footprint; use the 16-bit→1.58-bit transition schedule.

# 33. Head-wise attention sharing
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.11819)
- Share attention parameters across heads/layers where redundancy analysis shows near-duplicate heads. Reclaim those params for FFN/memory capacity.

# 34. Width-asymmetric FFN (wide early, narrow late)
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.14531)
- Early layers do feature extraction (need width); late layers refine (need depth). Taper FFN expansion ratio from 4x down to 2x across depth instead of uniform allocation.

# 35. Trained register/scratchpad tokens
- (idea)
- Prepend 16 learned "register" tokens that carry no text but give attention a persistent workspace. Nearly free parameters; documented to stabilize and improve transformer reasoning.

# 36. Entropy-gated early exit
- (idea)
- Add lightweight exit heads at 1/3 and 2/3 depth; easy tokens exit early. Saved inference compute funds more loops (idea #23) on hard tokens — compute allocated by difficulty.

# 37. Separate "knowledge neck" for retrieval injection
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.04426)
- One dedicated cross-attention layer mid-network reads retrieved passages (RETRO-lite: single layer, not interleaved). Minimal param cost; clean interface between parametric reasoning and non-parametric knowledge.

# 38. QK-norm + zero-init residual gates for deep-thin stability
- (idea)
- 40+ layer thin models are unstable; QK normalization and zero-initialized residual gates (ReZero-style) are near-free changes that keep very deep tiny models trainable at high LR.

# 39. Logit-softcap and z-loss for small-model calibration
- (idea)
- Gemma-style logit soft-capping plus z-loss regularization. Small models overconfidently spike logits; capping improves both training stability and downstream calibration for ~zero cost.

# 40. Recycled KV cache as working memory across turns
- (idea)
- Persist and re-attend to compressed KV summaries of earlier conversation turns instead of re-encoding text. Effective long-term memory for a model too small to internalize the session.

### Training & Distillation (41–70)

# 41. Reverse-KL distillation from a 4–9B teacher
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08543)
- MiniLLM-style reverse KL so our tiny student commits capacity to the teacher's modes, not its tail. Teacher: Gemma-class open model; this is the main training objective after the LM warm-up.

# 42. Ensemble-teacher distillation
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.02019)
- Baby Llama showed ensemble distillation beats any single teacher at 58M scale. Blend 2–3 diverse open teachers' distributions (after tokenizer alignment, idea #44).

# 43. Attention-relation distillation (architecture-agnostic)
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10957)
- MiniLM-style Q-K/V-V relation matching from the teacher's last layer only — works despite our exotic student architecture (loops, MoE) because it doesn't require layer-to-layer correspondence.

# 44. Universal-logit distillation across mismatched tokenizers
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.13765)
- Optimal-transport-based logit alignment so we can distill from teachers with different vocabularies. Unlocks ensemble idea #42 without forcing one tokenizer.

# 45. On-policy distillation loop
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2509.26497)
- Student generates, teacher scores/corrects each chunk, student trains on dense per-token teacher feedback. Fixes exposure bias that plain sequence distillation leaves behind; cheap because the student is tiny.

# 46. Shear-then-distill from an open 1–2B model
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06694)
- Structured-prune a strong open 1.4B down to ~100M (Sheared-LLaMA recipe), then continue with distillation. Inherits trained circuits at ~3% of from-scratch compute — likely the strongest single recipe available to us.

# 47. Massive overtraining: 100–300x Chinchilla
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08540)
- 100M model, 200–600B tokens (multi-epoch over curated data). Loss keeps dropping predictably past "optimal"; inference cost of a tiny model makes the trade trivially worth it.

# 48. muP for hyperparameter transfer from 10M proxies
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10545v1)
- Tune LR/init/batch on 10M-param proxies under maximal-update parameterization, transfer to 100M exactly. Spends ablation compute at 1/10th cost.

# 49. WSD schedule with branched anneals
- (idea)
- Warmup-stable-decay LR: hold a stable plateau, then branch multiple cheap anneals on different data mixes from one checkpoint. Lets us A/B final-stage mixes (idea #18) without retraining the trunk.

# 50. Rationale distillation with answer-only inference
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09629 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.11045)
- Train on teacher chain-of-thought, but also train a compressed "direct answer" mode from the same examples. Reasoning shapes the weights during training; inference stays short for easy queries.

# 51. Self-consistency-filtered synthetic targets
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12309)
- When generating training data with a teacher, sample N solutions, keep only majority-consistent answers as targets. Cheap correctness filter that sharply boosts synthetic-data quality.

# 52. Iterative self-improvement rounds at tiny scale
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14159)
- After distillation: student generates on training prompts, a verifier (teacher or unit tests) filters wins, student trains on its own filtered wins. STaR-style loops are affordable when the student costs pennies to sample.

# 53. Continual QAT schedule if going ternary
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11895)
- For idea #32: train 16-bit for the first ~60% of tokens, transition to 1.58-bit QAT for the rest. Documented to beat ternary-from-scratch across 11 tasks.

# 54. Knowledge-capacity checkpointing
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405)
- Probe checkpoints with a fixed synthetic fact-recall battery (bits stored per param) throughout training. Detects when knowledge absorption saturates — the signal to switch data stage or stop.

# 55. Curriculum temperature on teacher logits
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)
- Start distillation at high temperature (rich dark knowledge, easy targets), anneal toward low temperature (sharp decisions) late in training. Matches target difficulty to student maturity.

# 56. Hard-example mining from student perplexity
- (idea)
- Continuously oversample training documents where student loss is high but teacher loss is low — the "learnable gap" region. Avoids wasting epochs on what's already learned or what's hopeless.

# 57. Critique-conditioned finetuning
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.19227)
- Teacher generates data tailored to observed student weaknesses (aligning teacher generation with student preferences/failures). The teacher adapts to the student, not just vice versa.

# 58. Embedding warm-start from a large model
- (idea)
- Initialize token embeddings from a strong open model's embeddings (projected down via PCA to our width). Embeddings encode enormous distributional knowledge; free transfer at step 0.

# 59. Batch-size ramp with sequence-length curriculum
- (idea)
- Start at 512-token sequences/small batches (fast, many updates), ramp to 4k/large batches late. Small models learn local structure first anyway; this matches compute spend to what's learnable.

# 60. Multi-stage distillation cascade (9B → 1B → 100M)
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.01108)
- Distill through an intermediate-size assistant rather than directly from a huge teacher. Documented "capacity gap" problem: students learn better from teachers nearer their own size.

# 61. DPO against the student's own failure modes
- (idea)
- Build preference pairs where "rejected" = actual student outputs that are fluent-but-wrong, "chosen" = teacher fixes. Targets the model's real error distribution, not generic preference data.

# 62. Replay-mixed post-training to prevent alignment tax
- (idea — builds on idea #9)
- Mix 10–20% pretraining replay into every SFT/DPO stage. Small models lose raw knowledge fastest during alignment; replay is the cheapest known mitigation.

# 63. Tokenizer fitted to the final data mix
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.20849)
- Train the tokenizer on the curated corpus itself (not generic web), optimizing tokens-per-byte on our actual distribution. Fewer tokens per fact = more facts per training step and per context window.

# 64. Grokking-friendly weight decay on algorithmic subskills
- (idea)
- Train arithmetic/logic subskills with elevated weight decay and extended steps to push past memorization into generalizing circuits (grokking regime). Small models can grok small algorithms; that's cheaper than storing all answer instances.

# 65. Loss-free load balancing if MoE (idea #29)
- (idea)
- Use bias-based expert routing balance instead of auxiliary load-balancing loss. At tiny expert sizes, aux-loss interference is proportionally larger; bias balancing sidesteps it.

# 66. Distill Gemma's refusal/safety behavior explicitly
- (idea — builds on idea #19)
- Include teacher safety responses in the distillation set. Safety behavior is product quality too, and small models won't learn it incidentally.

# 67. Two-pass reading: predict-then-reread objective
- (idea)
- For knowledge-dense documents, train pass 1 normally, then pass 2 on the same doc with higher loss weight on previously-missed tokens. Focused re-reading mimics how humans study; trivially implementable in the dataloader.

# 68. Train-time retrieval augmentation (RETRO-style) from the start
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.04426 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00004)
- Pretrain with the retrieval neck (idea #37) active against a curated 1B-token database, so the model learns to lean on retrieval instead of memorizing. Retro-li proves this works at small scale.

# 69. Gaussian-noise regularization on retrieved neighbors
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00004)
- Retro-li's trick: noise the neighbor embeddings during training so retrieval use is robust to imperfect/domain-shifted databases at deployment.

# 70. Checkpoint soup of anneal branches
- (idea — builds on idea #49)
- Weight-average the best 3–5 anneal branches (different final data mixes) into one model. Model souping is nearly free and reliably adds a point or two when branches share a trunk.

### Inference & System (71–85)

# 71. Best-of-N with a tiny learned verifier
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2411.19477v1)
- Sample N answers, rank with a 20M-param verifier head trained on correctness labels. Test-time scaling laws say quality grows predictably with N — rented intelligence for a model too small to own it.

# 72. Self-consistency voting for math/logic only
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12309)
- Route detected math/logic queries to k=8 sampled chains with majority vote; everything else greedy. Spend test-time compute only where it's known to pay.

# 73. Retrieval database as the knowledge store, model as the reasoner
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.04426)
- Ship the model with a compressed, curated ~1GB local database (Wikipedia + references). Division of labor: 100M params of language/reasoning + external facts ≈ a much larger model's effective knowledge.

# 74. Speculative self-drafting via early-exit
- (idea — builds on idea #36)
- Use the model's own early-exit head as the draft model for speculative decoding against its full-depth pass. One model, faster decoding, no second network.

# 75. Confidence-routed escalation to a big model
- (idea)
- Calibrated uncertainty head decides per-query: answer locally or escalate to an API model. The honest version of "close to Gemma quality": match it on the 80% the small model can do, delegate the rest, measure the routing rate.

# 76. KV-cache quantization to fund longer context
- (idea)
- 4-bit KV cache lets the small model hold 4x context in the same memory — and context is the small model's main substitute for parametric knowledge.

# 77. Prompt-engineered system persona tuned for the model's limits
- (idea)
- Ship a default system prompt that steers toward the model's strengths (concise answers, asks clarifying questions, cites retrieval). Free quality; small models are disproportionately steerable by prompts they were post-trained with.

# 78. Per-domain adapter packs
- (idea)
- Tiny LoRA packs (1–2M params each) for domains like medical, legal, code — hot-swapped at inference based on a classifier. The base model stays general; specialization is loaded on demand instead of stored permanently.

# 79. Structured-output grammar constraints
- (idea)
- Constrained decoding (JSON schema, grammar) at inference. Small models gain disproportionately from pruning invalid continuations — the sampler does work the weights can't.

# 80. Iterative refinement mode (draft → critique → revise)
- (idea — builds on idea #16)
- Post-train an explicit revise-own-draft behavior; at inference, run 2 passes on hard queries. Sequential test-time compute that the self-correction training data (idea #16) directly enables.

# 81. Loop-count as a user-facing "thinking" dial
- (idea — builds on idea #23)
- Expose latent-loop iterations as low/medium/high thinking effort. Same weights, graded quality-latency tradeoff, mirrors frontier "thinking budgets."

# 82. Logit fusion with a cached n-gram model
- (idea)
- Interpolate model logits with a large local n-gram/kNN-LM store at inference. kNN-LM-style fusion adds factual recall without any training — the n-gram store remembers what 100M params can't.

# 83. Session memory distillation
- (idea — builds on idea #40)
- Background-summarize each conversation into structured notes the model retrieves in later sessions. Long-term personalization without finetuning.

# 84. Sparse-friendly deployment if ternary
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.05168)
- Ternary weights are naturally sparse-friendly (many exact zeros); pair 1.58-bit weights with 2:4 semi-structured sparsity kernels for another ~1.5x speedup at deployment.

# 85. Eval harness mirroring Gemma E4B head-to-head
- (idea)
- Continuous benchmark suite scoring our checkpoints against Gemma E4B on identical prompts (MMLU, GSM8K, ARC, HellaSwag, IFEval, human preference). "Close to Gemma" must be a measured number per capability, not a vibe — and it feeds the data loop (idea #18).

### Wildcards & Research Bets (86–100)

# 86. Hash-embedding vocabulary compression
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871)
- Replace the embedding table with hashed compositional embeddings (each token = sum of k shared hash-bucket vectors). Cuts embedding params 5–10x; spend the savings on depth.

# 87. Curriculum-grown depth (progressive stacking)
- (idea)
- Train 12 layers, duplicate to 24, continue, duplicate to 48. Progressive stacking historically cuts pretraining cost ~25–40% and suits deep-thin targets (idea #21).

# 88. Knowledge neurons audit + targeted re-injection
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405)
- Probe which fact categories the final model lost; generate focused synthetic data for exactly those holes; brief repair finetune with replay (idea #62). Treat knowledge as an inventory with restocking.

# 89. Latent chain-of-thought compression
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171)
- Distill teacher token-level CoT into the student's loop iterations (continuous latent reasoning) instead of generated text. Thinking without paying output tokens — risky but high payoff at small scale.

# 90. Tokenizer-free character model for the last mile
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10322v2)
- Hierarchical byte→word model variant as a parallel bet: perfect robustness to typos/casing/rare strings, zero embedding table. If BLT-style patching works at 100M, it wins the parameter budget war.

# 91. Modular two-tower: language core + swappable knowledge bank
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.01178)
- 70M "language/reasoning core" + 30M sparse memory bank (idea #28) trained to be re-writable post-hoc (memory editing). Update facts after shipping without touching the core.

# 92. Train-time dropout of retrieval to force dual competence
- (idea — builds on idea #68)
- Randomly disable retrieval for 30% of training so the model works degraded-but-sane offline, and learns what it does/doesn't know (improves routing idea #75).

# 93. Distill from a reasoning-RL teacher's pruned traces
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24945)
- Take R1-style teacher reasoning traces, prune redundant steps with the teacher itself, distill the minimal trace. Sub-billion reasoners (MobileLLM-R1) prove the ceiling is higher than assumed; trace length is the bottleneck for tiny students.

# 94. Synthetic "society of mind" dialogues
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.01663)
- Generate multi-agent debate transcripts (proposer/critic/judge) as training data so a single small model internalizes the critic role. CMAT-style collaboration distilled into one network.

# 95. Anti-curriculum on noise tolerance, late
- (idea)
- Last 5% of training: reintroduce noisy/messy real text (typos, OCR errors, informal chat). Pure clean curated data leaves a brittleness gap with real users; sand off the distribution mismatch at the end.

# 96. Bit-level knowledge accounting dashboard
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405)
- Operationalize the 2-bits/param law: running estimate of facts-stored vs. capacity throughout training, per domain. Decide data-mix changes from measured capacity utilization, not intuition.

# 97. Dual-objective: LM loss + contrastive fact-retrieval loss
- (idea)
- Auxiliary contrastive head pulls representations of (question, supporting-fact) pairs together during pretraining. Doubles use of the same tokens: generation skill + retrieval-quality embeddings (serves ideas #73/#82) from one model.

# 98. Genetic/evolutionary merge of specialized variants
- (idea — builds on idea #70)
- Train short specialist branches (math, code, chat) off the trunk, then evolutionary-search merge weights (evolutionary model merging) rather than uniform souping. Finds nonlinear merge recipes souping misses.

# 99. Overtrain a 50M twin as the ablation oracle
- (idea — builds on https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08540 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10545v1)
- Maintain a half-scale twin trained identically; run every risky intervention there first at 2x speed. Reliable-scaling results say 50M→100M deltas transfer; this is our cheap crystal ball.

# 100. The "knowledge sommelier" pipeline: every token earns its place
- (idea — synthesis of #1–#20)
- End-to-end gate: every candidate training document must pass fact-density (#3), dedup (#8), model-based filter (#4), and marginal-utility scoring against current checkpoint weaknesses (#18) before entering the mix. At 100M params, data admission is the product decision — run it like one.
